title: Control of torpedo grass in annual crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of torpedo grass in annual crop fields - Vietnam
Panicum repens Cỏ gừng, cỏ gừng bò, cỏ cựa gà, cỏ ống

Prevention: Clean equipment and farm machinery after working in an infested area to prevent rhizomes from being spread.
Do not accept potentially contaminated plant materials.
Limit the presence of open and disturbed areas by preventing overgrazing.
Control established populations of the weeds near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events.
P. repens translocated herbicides should be used in sufficient doses to target the rhizomes.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: annual crops such as vegetables, maize, and cassava.
Perennial grass with flowering stems (up to 1m high) arising from robust, creeping underground stems.
Flat or folded along the central vein (7–25cm long and 2–8mm wide), in 2 opposed rows along the stem.
Inflorescences branched (7– 22cm long) with upward-pointing flowerheads ('branches', each ca. 2-19cm long).
Survey fields weekly, including the edges, and consider direct control when found.
Look out for the weed in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread rhizome fragments
Direct Control: The species is difficult to control using mechanical means only.
Cutting, burning and hand- weeding are likely to result in strong and rapid regrowth from rhizome fragments.
Tillage must be deep in order to disturb as many of the rhizomes as possible.
Do this under dry conditions so the exposed rhizomes desiccate.
Use legumes as cover crops to smother the weed.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Atrazine (1200-2000 g a.i/ha for maize, and 1800-2400 g a.i/ha for sugarcane) or
WHO III (slightly hazardous), WSSA resistance group 7.
Apply 2-5 days after sowing for soybean, 5-10 days after sowing for groundnut.
Do not use for other crops.

emergence herbicide for annual crops, except in maize and sugar cane.
